tasks.instruction: Restore Version.bump_build. Increment the rightmost numeric run in an existing build field. If missing, default to build.1 or the supplied token followed by .1. Preserve release and prerelease fields, the old field when it has no digits, and the public signature.

Fix prerelease ordering used by Version.compare. Compare dot-separated identifiers in order. Numeric segments compare as numbers and sort below nonnumeric segments. Nonnumeric segments compare lexically. An exhausted equal prefix sorts below the longer sequence. Preserve build metadata and normal release precedence behavior of compare.

Restore Version.next_version(part, prerelease_token='rc') for major, minor, patch and prerelease. When the version is already a prerelease and the selected release part is the only outstanding bump, finalize the current release. Bumping an existing prerelease increments its last numeric run; a new prerelease starts on the next patch. Preserve the documented behavior of other parts.

Restore matching for semantic-version expressions with ==, !=, <, <=, > and >=. A plain version means equality. Reuse the release precedence rules, including prerelease ordering and ignoring build metadata.

Restore Version.bump_prerelease. Reuse the existing prerelease when present, incrementing its rightmost numeric run. A new prerelease defaults to rc.1; a nonempty supplied token replaces rc. Drop build metadata and preserve the release version. Keep the existing public signature and handle empty tokens.

Restore English ordinal suffixes in ordinal(value, gender='male'). Integers ending in 1, 2 and 3 get st, nd and rd, except the teens. Keep the existing function signature and fallback behavior for nonintegral inputs.

Restore readable file sizes. Preserve single-byte pluralization, decimal, binary IEC, and GNU units; keep negative values and the existing format option. Keep the public signature and default formatting.

Restore grouped thousands in intcomma. Preserve negative signs, decimal suffixes, optional rounding with ndigits, and numeric strings. Keep the documented formatting behavior for values that cannot be grouped.
Restore AP-style English number formatting. Convert integers zero through nine, including integer strings, to words. Preserve readable text and other numbers, keeping the existing public function.
